grade.basis: Only three frames were available, but the writing is clearly readable: Bass I moves in tenor and treble clef in the high register, with fast sixteenth-note runs and chromatic figures in Allegro moderato, trills, and tenor-clef passages with wide leaps and accented, shifting lines. This is sustained professional-grade solo-bass writing in the upper register; the ensemble is three equal, interlocking parts.

Only No. 4 (All'Albanese) was in the supplied parts. Violin 1 is mostly quarter and half notes in B-flat and G major, with short stepwise eighth and sixteenth groups, a few high notes around third position, some double-stops and a few accidentals. Violin 2 adds a repeated tremolo double-stop passage and pizzicato; the parts are written for teaching and ensemble use.

Cello I carries the melody in the high register throughout Religioso, with sustained lines on many leger lines, and in the Nocturne it moves into tenor and treble clef. It also has chromatic turns, a rapid sixteenth-note passage, and long cantabile phrases that need secure thumb-position intonation. The lower three parts are far simpler, sustained and supportive, in the first few positions.
